relevance_note: The paper reports an Italian family in which four members carry a novel heterozygous TNFAIP3 frameshift variant, described as 'four family members carrying a novel mutation in the TNFAIP3 gene leading to HA20'.
method_note: Read the paper, the schema and the rules directly; no script transcribed the tables, so every quote below was copied by hand from the Markdown. Table 1 lists one row per patient per manifestation and repeats the patient label in every row, so it contains no stacked (' / ') cells and every value could be attributed to a named patient. Uncertainties and contradictions found: (1) the text says Pt4's 'adult height is 10-20° centile' while Table 1 gives 'Short stature (10-25°)'; (2) the abstract calls the four patients 'consanguineous' while the rest of the paper describes only an Italian family - consanguinity 'yes' rests on the abstract wording alone; (3) Pt2 and Pt3 are said to carry 'the same frameshift mutation' as Pt1 and Pt4 (confirmed by Sanger sequencing), so the printed strings c.1727dupC / p.His577Alafs*95 / NM_006290 were recorded for them too, although the variant string itself is printed only in the sentence about Pt1 and Pt 4; (4) age at onset is printed only as 'Early childhood (less than 2 years)', an upper bound, so no ISO 8601 duration was given for onset; (5) 'Pt3 was the only with a classical, albeit mild, autoinflammatory phenotype (transient recurrent episodes of fevers) and no autoimmune manifestation up to the age of 14' was used to exclude autoimmune thyroiditis, type 1 diabetes, autoimmune hepatitis and autoimmune cytopenia for Pt3, but not arthritis (HA20 arthritis is also described as autoinflammatory); (6) the father appears only as 'a relative (father)' in the legends of Figures 3 and 4 and is included as a relative; no TNFAIP3 variant is stated for him (trio WES was performed on Pt1 and her parents and the variant was found in Pt1 and the mother only); (7) age at diagnosis was recorded only for Pt4 (thyroiditis diagnosed at the age of 41), because no age at HA20 diagnosis is given for anyone; (8) the 'ANA negative', 'dsDNA negative' and 'ENA negative' cells and the normal GH secretion tests were recorded as excluded findings under D-27, naming the abnormality they rule out; Pt1's 'not associated with recurrent infection' was recorded as excluded 'recurrent infections'; (9) 'After 9 months, she does not show signs of active arthritis' (Pt2) was treated as treatment response, not as absence of arthritis; (10) no study inclusion or exclusion criterion was used as evidence about a person.
